subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap Skyline Analytics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@skyline.ai>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@skyline.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap Skyline Analytics

Hi Elena / Tom

Thanks again for your time this morning. Below is a short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum. Please correct anything I missed.

Summary / pain points
- Spikes in inference traffic during end-of-day batch scoring and ad-hoc analytics runs are causing inconsistent latency for product features (notably the recommendation engine).
- Current stack: AWS SageMaker endpoints + in-house queuing layer. You see 95th-99th percentile latencies spike >1s during peaks and retry logic is adding cost.
- Isolation requirement: certain models process PII and finance data; compliance team requires tenant isolation and audit logs.

Goals / success criteria
- Predictable sustained TPS: ~500-1,000 TPS for generation workloads with headroom for 2x burst.
- P99 latency target for production routes: <150ms for typical generation prompts.
- Dedicated GPU pools (customer-isolated) to satisfy compliance and limit noisy-neighbor interference.
- Autoscaling behavior: fast scale-up for short bursts; warm pool to avoid cold-start latency for critical requests.

Fit with Redwood Dedicated
- Dedicated reserved GPU pools provide the isolation you need plus predictable throughput.
- Smart warm-pool + auto-burst policies give the fast ramp you described while keeping unit costs more predictable than ad-hoc on-demand provisioning.

Immediate next steps
1) I attached a preliminary capacity estimate (capacity_estimate.xlsx) with two sizing options (baseline and burst-ready) Rafael and Marcus will refine after the technical deep-dive.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra and security folks to confirm network/KMS/QoS constraints (Marcus to lead).
3) I'll share a draft SOW and an initial pricing ballpark for reserved capacity after we align on sizing.

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive:
- Thu 6/18 10:00-11:00 PT
- Fri 6/19 09:00-10:00 PT

Please let me know which time works or propose alternatives. Also looping Rafael (AE) and Marcus (SE) to track pricing and technical questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Office: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: capacity_estimate.xlsx

From: Elena Park <elena.park@skyline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Wu <tom.wu@skyline.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap Skyline Analytics

Thanks Marissa this is very helpful and accurate. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Priority is definitely latency consistency for the customer-facing recommendation API, and isolation for models that touch PII.
- On autoscaling: curious how "burst-ready" works in practice. How quickly can you scale up to handle a sudden 2x spike? Do you rely on a warm pool or instant provisioning?
- Can you share a rough pricing ballpark for the baseline vs burst-ready sizing so we can validate internally before the technical deep-dive? Procurement will want a rough number.

For the deep-dive, Thu 6/18 10:00 PT works for us I’ll invite our infra lead (Security cc: sarah.kim@skyline.ai) and procurement (procurement@skyline.ai).

Appreciate the quick turnaround, looking forward to the SOW draft.

Best,
Elena
Director of Engineering | Skyline Analytics
elena.park@skyline.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@skyline.ai>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@skyline.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap Skyline Analytics

Thanks Elena great. Quick answers and next steps: 

Autoscaling / burst behavior:
- We support a configurable warm pool (pre-warmed GPUs) that covers a portion of expected burst traffic; for additional burst we use fast provisioned nodes with optimized image layering so most scale-ups are within ~60-90 seconds for additional capacity. For very latency-sensitive routes we recommend a larger warm pool to keep p99s under 150ms. Marcus can share telemetry from similar customers in the tech deep-dive.

Pricing ballpark:
- Baseline option (reserved pool sized for sustained 500 TPS): ballpark $XXk/mo (capacity + infra + basic support).
- Burst-ready option (reserved pool + 40% warm pool + burst credits): ballpark $YYk/mo.
(We'll provide a detailed, line-item estimate after Marcus confirms sizing.)

Next steps / calendar:
- Technical deep-dive confirmed: Thu 2026-06-18 10:00-11:00 PT (Marcus to share dial-in). Please include Sarah Kim (security) and one person from procurement.
- I attached a draft SOW (SOW-draft.pdf) and included a HubSpot link + DocuSign for an initial MSA if you want to start procurement early.

If you want, Rafael and I can also run a 30-minute cost/roi review for procurement after the sizing is finalized.

Thanks see you on Thursday.

Best,
